title: Prima Mente Launches Alzheimer's AI Competition With 150M Cell Atlas
summary:
An international team of biotech and technology firms are offering AI researchers access to specialized brain cell data to find new drug targets. The Alzheimer's Translation Challenge, led by Prima Mente and AlzData, uses a 150M cell atlas of neurons, astrocytes, and microglia to identify new therapeutic hypotheses for the disease. Winning participants will have their AI models validated in Prima Mente's wet lab to confirm predicted molecular and functional effects.

The competition begins in spring 2027, with registration currently open via the AD workbench and Hugging Face. Partners providing data and computational infrastructure include Nvidia, Nebius AI, Talisman Therapeutics, Ultima Genomics, Cellanome, Prime Intellect, and Boltz Bio. The effort follows a recent discovery of a new class of Alzheimer's biomarkers by Goodfire AI and Prima Mente.

selectedTweets.text:
Today we're launching the Alzheimer's Translation Challenge, a global AI competition to discover new therapeutic hypotheses for Alzheimer's disease.

At its core is a new 150M cell atlas of neurons, astrocytes, and microglia across different genetic backgrounds under combinatorial perturbations, with multi-modal readouts. 

The data will be made available through the AD workbench, Hugging Face and Prima Mente's modeling platform.

The challenge is led by @PrimaMente and @AlzData in collaboration with @nvidia, @huggingface, @nebiusai, Talisman Therapeutics, @UltimaGenomics, @cellanome, @PrimeIntellect, @GoodfireAI, and @boltz_bio.

In 1906, Alois Alzheimer described a new disease of the brain. After 120 years of progress, we still don't fully understand what drives this disease. We want to change that.

Participants will use the dataset to build AI models, assessed through a series of evals from general benchmarks to more complex tasks. 

Top teams will be shortlisted, and their experimental hypotheses tested in Prima Mente's wet lab. Teams win when their hypotheses demonstrate the predicted molecular and functional effect.
